principles: Never leave or commit git conflict markers in machine-generated story metadata
Serialize the reconcile (main commit + merge) under the main-write-lock so concurrent main commits cannot race it
Deterministic resolution is valid because story metadata is machine-generated (post-advance state is authoritative)
Minimal change to the reconcile; no INIT_CHECK semantic change; idempotent on retry; single-session flow byte-identical
drivers: The corruption hit twice this session and broke the CLI (could not parse the story)
Concurrent main-branch churn races the reconcile's git merge
The main-write-lock already exists (B-f60c) but is not applied to this path

options.name: A: lock + deterministic metadata resolution
pros: Lock prevents the race; deterministic resolution handles any residual conflict
Never leaves markers, never strands the user
cons: Slightly more code than lock-only (must resolve conflicted metadata paths)

options.name: B: lock + abort-and-recover
pros: Simpler conflict branch (git merge --abort + recovery error)
cons: Strands the user on a conflict (must re-run); worse UX for a machine-resolvable conflict

options.name: C: lock only (assume no conflict)
cons: A conflict from legitimate pre-existing divergence can still leave markers; doesn't fully close the bug

rationale: Option A wraps the reconcile (main commit + merge) in withReentrantMainWriteLock to prevent the race, AND on any residual merge conflict resolves all conflicted story-metadata paths deterministically to the authoritative post-advance state, so the reconcile never leaves markers and never strands the user. C (lock only) doesn't handle a conflict from legitimate divergence; B (abort-and-recover) is a worse UX for a machine-resolvable conflict. A repro test pins the behavior before the fix.

preMortem.scenario: Deterministic resolution picks the wrong side
preMortem.trigger: resolving to the story-branch version instead of the post-advance main version
preMortem.mitigation: story metadata is machine-generated; resolve to the post-INIT_CHECK (main-committed) version; test asserts the resolved index.json equals the expected post-advance state

preMortem.trigger: the reconcile runs inside a context already holding the main-write-lock
preMortem.mitigation: use withReentrantMainWriteLock; test that a normal single-session advance does not deadlock

preMortem.trigger: multiple story-metadata files conflict in the merge
preMortem.consequence: partial resolution leaves markers in another file
preMortem.mitigation: resolve ALL conflicted paths under the storyDir deterministically; test a multi-file metadata conflict

preMortem.scenario: Lock not released on error → stuck lock
preMortem.mitigation: withMainWriteLock releases in finally on throw; doctor stuck-lock check (B-f60c) covers residue
